# dev-diagnosis

> One offline CLI that diagnoses a repo the way four small tools do: context
> noise for AI agents, missing CLI commands, build-cache value, and flaky
> tests. No dependencies, no network, Node >= 18.

## When to reach for it

- Just took over a repo and want to know what is wrong with it: `dev-diagnosis all`
- An AI agent keeps reading huge data dumps, logs or lockfiles: `dev-diagnosis context`
- A command works in the terminal but not in the IDE or CI: `dev-diagnosis path <name>`
- Builds feel slow even with a cache: `dev-diagnosis cache -- <build-command>`
- CI goes red, then green on retry: `dev-diagnosis flakes <junit-runs-dir>`

## Install and run

```sh
npx dev-diagnosis-cli
```

Or install once and use it anywhere:

```sh
npm install -g dev-diagnosis-cli
dev-diagnosis all
```

`dev-diagnosis` with no arguments is the same as `dev-diagnosis all` on the
current directory. `dev-diagnosis all [path] --command <name> --flakes <dir>
-- <build-command...>` runs every check that has its input. `--json` gives
machine-readable output. `context --fix` writes the suggestions into
`<path>/.aiignore` and re-scans; a clean re-scan exits 0. Exit codes: 0 all
checks that ran passed, 1 something found to fix or could not run, 2 usage
error. `all` ends with a one-line summary of passed / failed / skipped
checks, context noise found, and cache savings.

## Let an agent run it

- `dev-diagnosis setup` wires the tool into Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor
  and VS Code (preview first, never overwrites existing config).
- `dev-diagnosis --mcp` serves the same four checks as MCP tools over stdio
  (`diagnose_context`, `diagnose_path`, `diagnose_cache`, `diagnose_flakes`,
  `diagnose_all`); add `--sandbox <dir>` to keep it inside one repo.
- `dev-diagnosis --skill-generate` writes a SKILL.md telling an agent to run
  `dev-diagnosis all` when it starts work in a repo, fix what FAILs, and
  re-run to confirm. It never overwrites an existing SKILL.md.

## In CI

One step runs the diagnosis and fails the job when a check fails; it runs the
published npm package (`@latest`). The action is defined in `action.yml` at
the repo root:

```yaml
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dev-doctor@main
  with:
    path: .
    args: --command node
```
